sections: A.2 Selection under Matched and Shifted Targets

scope.paper_mechanism: Target-aware selection can correct a train-target gap; finite-budget gains and asymptotic improvements are distinct claims.
scope.miniature_comparison: Regularized logistic regression on all source samples or a target-probe-selected subset, across teacher angle, pool size, and label noise; random subsets are a control.
preserved_assumptions: Gaussian examples labeled by rotated source and target teachers.
Selection favors agreement with a target proxy and small proxy margins.
Shared source pool and fresh target evaluation samples across arms.
simplifications: 20 dimensions and two finite pool sizes replace asymptotic analysis.
A probe fitted on 40 target labels replaces access to the target teacher.
Fixed L2 penalties and retention policy, with a fallback to full data; no mixture experiment.
unsupported_claims: Asymptotic advancement or replication of LLM training results.
An equal-information selection advantage over a baseline trained only on source labels.

evidence.finding: The source studies target-aware selection and separates finite-budget from limiting behavior.
A finite-sample target probe drives selection, with variable retained counts and a full-pool fallback; this is an approximation with a narrower claim.
Only target_select uses the 40 target labels through a fitted probe; uniform and random_select fit source labels. The extra supervision must be accounted for or explicitly scoped.
Source pool, target probe set, and target test samples are drawn before the method branch, so matching seed/context shares these samples.
Random-subset selection has its own generator and does not perturb the shared test draws.
Target test features and labels are separate from pool and probe training. delta_test is test-derived auxiliary feedback, not a selector input in this implementation.
Primary accuracy uses clean target-teacher labels and is higher-better. Test-derived diagnostics must not be used for internal fit selection in a repair.
0.01 means one percentage point of target accuracy. Whether that is a meaningful tolerance for this miniature still needs justification; cached equivalence alone cannot justify it.
L-BFGS-B returns res.x without checking success or convergence. No new convergence, repeatability, or parameter-response probes were run.
Target supervision, variable subset size, and fallback can change the comparison.
The near-zero average pools teacher angles; it does not show there is no conditional effect or establish the paper asymptotic claim.

rationale: Assistant draft only. Resolve the target-label information asymmetry and limit the claim to a finite logistic-regression experiment. Check fit convergence, document the fallback, and justify the one-point margin.

assistant_assessment.evidence_scope: Primary method sections and static implementation inspected; historical caches analyzed. No new lab executions, parameter probes, independent confirmation, or model evaluations.
blockers: Resolve the target-label information asymmetry and limit the claim to a finite logistic-regression experiment.
Check fit convergence, document the fallback, and justify the one-point margin.
owner_actions: Compare source Figure 1e-f/A.2 to the finite probe policy and decide what can be claimed.
Consider a target-informed baseline/control in a new version if claiming equal-information improvement.
Probe zero-gap and shifted-gap behavior, full-pool fallback, and optimizer failures.
